0010.name: Frame-ready flag
desc: Handshake between the main loop and the NMI. The main loop clears it with STZ and spins until it is non-zero;
the NMI handler increments it when it finishes the frame's PPU work (also on the lag/Mode 7 tail path).
Reset code does INC once at boot so the first pass skips the wait.
Values: 0 = waiting for the next frame; non-zero = frame handled.

0011.name: IRQ split stage
desc: Which IRQ of the frame's screen split comes next. The NMI tail clears it to 0; the IRQ handler bumps it to 1
after the first split, so the second IRQ sets up the BG3 scroll/screen mode or the Mode 7 boss-room splits.
Values: 0 = first IRQ pending; 1 = second IRQ stage.

0012.name: Stripe image number
desc: Number of the stripe image queued for upload to VRAM; the upload routine uses it times 3 as an offset into
ImagePointers. Set by game modes and cutscenes to draw title screen, file select, overworld border, credits
backgrounds and so on, and consumed by the Upload stripe image routine.
Values: $03 = title screen; $06 = overworld border; $D2 = credits background; 0 = none queued (probably).

0013.name: Frame counter
desc: Free-running frame counter, incremented every frame by the main loop, including while the game is paused or
locked. Sprites and animations read low bits to pace things: 'every 32 frames' is [$13] & $1F == 0, Boo/bat
wobble, firework sparks, overworld water animation. Compare $0014, which stops when the game is frozen.
Values: wraps 00-FF.

0014.name: Frame counter B
desc: Second frame counter used for most sprite and Mario animation timing. It counts every frame the game is
running; sprite routines mask it (for example & $30) to time Chuck states, Lakitu's cloud, Yoshi's tongue
and the Boo stream. Level preparation clears bits 0-2 and 5-7 of it (TRB) to keep only bits 3-4.
Values: wraps 00-FF. See $0013 for the always-running counter.

0015.name: Controller 1 held (byetUDLR)
desc: Buttons held by the active player this frame: pad byte 1 ($0DA2) with the A and X bits of byte 2 merged into
bits 7 and 6, so jump (B or A) and run/fire (Y or X) each need one test. Read by Mario physics, swimming, cape
flight, carrying and menus; game mode 14 clears the Down bit while Mario is busy.
Bits: 7 = B or A; 6 = Y or X; 5 = Select; 4 = Start; 3 = Up; 2 = Down; 1 = Left; 0 = Right.

0016.name: Controller 1 newly pressed (byetUDLR)
desc: Buttons that went down this frame (current AND NOT previous) for pad byte 1, with a new X press merged into
bit 6 (A is not merged, see $0018). Used for one-shot actions: jump start, menu cursor, fireball and spin input.
Game mode 14 clears bit 6 here and in $0018 while Mario is busy.
Bits: 7 = B; 6 = Y or X; 5 = Select; 4 = Start; 3 = Up; 2 = Down; 1 = Left; 0 = Right.

0017.name: Controller 1 held (axlr----)
desc: Second joypad byte for the active player: A, X, L and R held. Written by the Read joypads routine, read by
Mario animation (spin jump, run), Yoshi poses, L/R scrolling and the title screen/demo code.
Bits: 7 = A; 6 = X; 5 = L; 4 = R; 3-0 unused.

0018.name: Controller 1 newly pressed (axlr----)
desc: Edge-detected version of $0017: A, X, L, R pressed this frame. Combined with $0016 (ORA) to catch a new B or A
press for jumping or swimming up, and used by the menu cursor and file menus (which OR in controller 2).

0019.name: Mario power-up
desc: Mario's current power-up state. Written when he is hit, collects a mushroom, flower, feather or star... and
when a level starts; read by collision, drawing, the cape-flight tables, sprite interactions and platform code.
Values: 0 = small; 1 = big; 2 = cape; 3 = fire flower.

001A.name: Layer 1 X position (low)
desc: Horizontal scroll of layer 1 (BG1) in pixels, also called the screen boundary X. $001B is the high byte. The
NMI copies it to the BG1 H-scroll register. Scroll code sets it from $1462 each frame; sprites, blocks and
particles subtract it to get on-screen X and delete themselves when off the screen. Cutscenes and the
overworld write it directly.

001B.name: Layer 1 X position (high)
desc: High byte of layer 1's horizontal scroll position ($001A is the low byte). Identifies the 256-pixel screen
page; sprites compare an object's X high byte against it to see if it is on the current page.

001C.name: Layer 1 Y position (low)
desc: Vertical scroll of layer 1 (BG1) in pixels; $001D is the high byte. Set by the scroll routine from $1464,
shifted by the layer-shake and cutscene code, and shipped to the BG1 V-scroll by the NMI. Sprites subtract
it to get screen Y; the overworld and credits code write it directly.

001D.name: Layer 1 Y position (high)
desc: High byte of layer 1's vertical scroll ($001C is the low byte). Saved and restored around code that borrows
the scroll position (Game mode 14 scroll shake, Directional Coins) and set in cutscenes.

001E.name: Layer 2 X position (low)
desc: Horizontal scroll of layer 2 (BG2, the background/second layer); $001F is the high byte. Written by the scroll
routine from $1466, zeroed by layer 2 scroll sprites and the ending scene, and used when generating Map16
tiles on layer 2. The NMI sends it to the BG2 H-scroll.

0020.name: Layer 2 Y position (low)
desc: Vertical scroll of layer 2 (BG2); $0021 is the high byte. Written by the scroll routine from $1468 and set at
level load from a per-level table; read by Map16 generation and the NMI (BG2 V-scroll).

0021.name: Layer 2 Y position (high)
desc: High byte of layer 2's vertical scroll ($0020 is the low byte). Cleared at level load and by cutscenes; the
NMI writes $0020/$0021 to the BG2 V-scroll register.

0022.name: Layer 3 X position (low)
desc: Horizontal scroll of layer 3 (BG3: status bar, message boxes, level layer 3 effects); $0023 is the high
byte. Set at level start to layer 1 X / 2, advanced by Layer 3 scroll handlers, cleared by message boxes and
the ending. The IRQ writes it to the BG3 H-scroll register.

0023.name: Layer 3 X position (high)
desc: High byte of the BG3 horizontal scroll ($0022 is the low byte). Cleared by the message box code and set to 1
by a Layer 3 scroll handler; the IRQ writes $0022/$0023 to BG3.

0024.name: Layer 3 Y position (low)
desc: Vertical scroll of layer 3 (BG3); $0025 is the high byte. Set at level setup, copied from layer 1 Y by a
scroll handler, moved by the credits scroll, and set from the fireball routine. The IRQ writes it to BG3.

0025.name: Layer 3 Y position (high)
desc: High byte of the BG3 vertical scroll ($0024 is the low byte). Cleared during layer 3 setup and by the
message box code; the IRQ writes $0024/$0025 to BG3.

0026.name: Layer 2 offset from layer 1, X (low)
desc: Layer 2 X position minus layer 1 X position (computed in the scroll routine; with layer 3 interaction it is
$0022 minus $1462). $0027 is the high byte. Interactions with a moving layer 2 add or subtract it: block-hit
hitboxes, sprites spawned from blocks, Mario level collision and sprite-block checks.

0027.name: Layer 2 offset from layer 1, X (high)
desc: High byte of the layer 2 minus layer 1 X offset ($0026 is the low byte). Added to or borrowed from a sprite's
or block's X high byte when positions are converted between layers.

0028.name: Layer 2 offset from layer 1, Y (low)
desc: Layer 2 Y position minus layer 1 Y position; $0029 is the high byte. Same role as $0026 but vertical, used by
block-hit hitboxes, sprite spawns from blocks, sprite-block interaction and Mario collision.

0029.name: Layer 2 offset from layer 1, Y (high)
desc: High byte of the layer 2 minus layer 1 Y offset ($0028 is the low byte). Added to or borrowed from Y high bytes
when converting positions between layers.

002A.name: Mode 7 center X (low)
desc: Mode 7 rotation center X; $002B is the high byte. The NMI adds $0080 and writes it to the Mode 7 center
register $211F. Boss rooms set it to $0080. The Reznor code reuses it as the circle center X of the
Reznor ring.

002B.name: Mode 7 center X (high)
desc: High byte of the Mode 7 / Reznor ring center X ($002A is the low byte). Zeroed along with $002A.

002C.name: Mode 7 center Y (low)
desc: Mode 7 rotation center Y ($002D is the high byte). Sent to $2120 after adding $0080 by the NMI. Set to $0050
at Mario Start, $00A0 in boss rooms and $00C8 by the Bowser fight; Reznor code uses it as ring center Y.

002E.name: Mode 7 matrix A
desc: Mode 7 matrix parameter A, calculated as cos(angle) * scale by the Calculate Mode 7 rotation matrix routine
from $0036 and $0038. $0034 gets a copy as matrix D. The NMI writes it to $211B.

0030.name: Mode 7 matrix B
desc: Mode 7 matrix parameter B, sin(angle) * scale from the matrix routine. $0032 (matrix C) is its negation.
The NMI writes it to $211C.

0036.name: Mode 7 rotation angle
desc: Angle of the rotating/tilting Mode 7 picture, 9 bits ($0000-$01FF, high byte $0037). Input to the rotation
matrix routine. Koopaling and Bowser fights change it: the tilting platform, Ludwig's and Koopa Kid's rooms,
and Bowser's bounce. Mario's platform/ceiling collision reads it as the tilt.
Values: 0 = not rotated.

0037.name: Mode 7 rotation angle (high)
desc: High byte (bit 0 only is used) of the Mode 7 rotation angle ($0036 is the low byte). Non-zero together with
$0036 means the room is rotated; Koopaling code ORs the two to decide whether to keep turning.

0038.name: Mode 7 scale
desc: Scale for the Mode 7 picture's matrix A/B ($0039 does C/D). Boss fights change it: Bowser increments it, Ludwig's
code decrements it as a room parameter. The matrix routine multiplies by it.

0039.name: Mode 7 scale (second)
desc: Second Mode 7 scale value, used for matrix parameters C and D; Mario Start sets it to $20. Boss code reuses it
as a stepping value (Ludwig decrement, Koopa Kid tilt step * 2, Bowser's bounce increment).

003A.name: Mode 7 scroll X
desc: Mode 7 scroll X, written to the Mode 7 H-offset ($210D). Boss rooms set it to $0080; Position Mode 7 picture
writes [$3A+X] as -A + a table value + the layer 1 screen boundary (X = 0: horizontal, X = 2: vertical).

003E.name: BGMODE mirror
desc: Shadow of the BG mode / character size register ($2105), written by the NMI. Normally $09: Mode 1 with BG3
on top; level end ORs $08 for BG3 priority.
Values: $09 = Mode 1, BG3 priority.

003F.name: OAM address (priority index)
desc: Value written to the OAM address register ($2102) after the OAM DMA, setting which sprite has priority. The
upload routine clears it to 0; Mario Start sets $C8 and the overworld loader $F0.

0040.name: Color math mirror (CGADSUB)
desc: Shadow of the color math add/subtract control ($2131). Boss fades, spotlight effects and the Mario Start
screen set it; the NMI writes it (with bit 2 masked) to $2131.
Values: $24 = color math on BG3 and backdrop; $34 = also on sprites.

0041.name: Window mask mirror, BG1/BG2
desc: Shadow of $2123: window masks for BG1 and BG2. Cleared on screen reset; set for the iris-out and keyhole
effects, Mario Start and the controller detect screen. The NMI writes it to $2123.
Values: $22 or $33 are used for keyhole/iris windows; 0 = no window.

0042.name: Window mask mirror, BG3/BG4
desc: Shadow of $2124: window masks for BG3 and BG4. Cleared on screen reset and by the lives exchange; keyhole and
iris-out effects set it. The NMI writes it to $2124.

0043.name: Window mask mirror, OBJ/color
desc: Shadow of $2125: window masks for sprites and the color window. Set by Mario Start, the overworld loader,
keyhole/iris effects and the dark-room spotlight ($20: color window uses window 1); the NMI writes it to $2125.

0044.name: Color math select mirror (CGWSEL)
desc: Shadow of $2130: color window control and subscreen select. Reset to $02 on screen reset; effects set it
(spotlight $20 = color math only outside the window). The NMI writes it to $2130.

0045.name: Layer 1 tile column range, left
desc: Left edge of the range of Map16 columns to update on layer 1, computed as screen X / 16 - 8. Pairs with $0047
(right edge). Indexed by $0055 in the Layer 2 update table builders, so $0045,X is the left edge for layer
[X]. Scroll sprites also set [$45+L] = $FFF8.

0047.name: Layer 1 tile column range, right
desc: Right edge of the Map16 column range to update on layer 1, screen X / 16 + $17 ($0045 is the left edge).
At level load it starts as a copy of $0045 and is incremented while columns are built. The overworld
setup uses it for a row counter that starts at $20.

0049.name: Layer 2 tile column range, left
desc: Left edge of the Map16 column range for layer 2 (partner of $0045 for layer 1), computed in the tile range
setup and read by the Layer 2 update table and stripe builders, indexed by X.
